requirement_text.REQ-044: Pure transition kernel core types and dispatch skeleton. 6 acceptance criteria: (1) zero Repo/HTTP/file/clock calls in transition/3's call graph, (2) determinism demonstrated by an explicit test, (3) unknown event type and unknown node_id both return errors naming specifics, never raise, (4) HUMAN_TASK adds to pending_task_nodes while START/END/EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY/PARALLEL_GATEWAY do not -- each of the five node-type cases has its own explicit test, (5) moduledoc states the Zig ObjectMap divergence, (6) reuses REQ-028's graph structs, no redefinition.

task.description: WF-02 Step 3b hard gate (docs/agents/workflows/WF-02_requirement_implementation.md 'Step 3b — Test design gate') and your own role file .claude/agents/test-design-validator.md. Read test/specs/REQ-044.md and the 3 test files independently -- do not read TEST-DESIGNER's handoff summary as a substitute. Run mix test test/letflow/engine/ yourself and confirm the actual pass count. Perform at least one real mutation check (per the project's established precedent, e.g. REQ-034's WF02 run) on a load-bearing assertion (the determinism property test or one of the error-path tests) -- deliberately break the corresponding implementation code, confirm the test actually fails, then revert cleanly and re-confirm green.
acceptance_criteria: Every acceptance criterion has >=1 runnable test targeting it -- no @tag :skip without a passing counterpart
No TODO: implement test left in the spec
Test fixtures use per-test unique data, no cross-test pollution
Tests are self-sufficient -- don't depend on other tests running first
No hardcoded secrets/connection strings in test files
At least one real mutation-testing drill performed and reported: which line was mutated, which test(s) caught it, tree reverted cleanly afterward

result.summary: Independently read test/specs/REQ-044.md (all 458 lines) and the 3 test files (transition_test.exs 405 lines, instance_state_test.exs 33 lines, token_test.exs 26 lines) directly, plus lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex to cross-check assertions against real implementation. All 6 ACs have >=1 dedicated runnable test: AC2 determinism via a StreamData property test (world_generator/0, max_runs: 150) spanning every dispatch path; AC3's two named error paths (unknown_event_type via a bare-tuple test + a 5-shape non-tuple loop test; unknown_node_id via two tests including exact-id-echo) plus a defensive unknown_token_id test; AC4's 5-way dispatch each in its own describe block (START, END, HUMAN_TASK, EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY, PARALLEL_GATEWAY) plus a beyond-AC catch-all test for SERVICE_TASK/TIMER/SUB_PROCESS/bogus atom; AC1/AC5/AC6 are structural/prose criteria correctly verified by inspection (grep + mix xref quoted output, direct moduledoc reading, structural argument) rather than manufactured ExUnit busywork, matching REQ-028's established AC5 precedent. No @tag :skip anywhere, no 'TODO: implement test' text in the spec (grep confirmed empty). No hardcoded secrets/connection strings in any of the 3 test files (grep confirmed empty). Every fixture is built fresh per-test via local helper functions (node/2, edge/3, graph/2, token/2, instance_state/2) from in-memory structs only -- no shared mutable state, no DB rows, no cross-test ordering dependency; async: true is justified (no Repo/Ecto.Sandbox anywhere in lib/letflow/engine/, independently re-grepped). Ran `mix test test/letflow/engine/` myself: real output '1 property, 19 tests, 0 failures', matching the spec's own claimed count -- not trusted from the spec alone. Mutation-testing drill: edited lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex line 141 inside transition/3's top-level case catch-all, changing `{:error, {:unknown_event_type, other}}` to `{:error, {:mutated_event_type, other}}`. Re-ran `mix test test/letflow/engine/`: 19 tests, 2 failures -- exactly the two AC3 'unknown event type' tests caught it (transition_test.exs:172 'a tuple with an unrecognized tag returns {:error, {:unknown_event_type, event}}, not a crash' and transition_test.exs:180 inside 'a non-tuple event value also returns {:error, {:unknown_event_type, event}}, not a crash'), all other 17 tests still passed, confirming the mutation was caught precisely by its intended targets and nothing else masked or over-triggered. Reverted via `git checkout -- lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex`; re-read the file to confirm line 141 restored to `{:error, {:unknown_event_type, other}}`; re-ran `mix test test/letflow/engine/`: 19 tests, 0 failures again. Final `git status` shows only the untracked handoff JSON for this step; `git diff --stat` is empty -- tree is clean, no leftover mutation.
